newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice prices nudge lower with dong decline.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice prices nudge lower with dong decline.

text.p: Vietnamese rice prices have fallen slightly this week following a sharp slide in the rate of the national currency against the dollar, traders said on Thursday.
They said five percent broken grade rice was trading at around $265-$268 per tonne FOB Saigon Port against recent steady levels of around $270.
Ten percent broken grade was quoted at $258-$261 per tonne.
Vietnam's normally stable currency, the dong, tumbled this week on the interbank market following a decision by the central bank to widen the permitted trading band.
Dealers said this coupled with higher prices of Thai rice was making Vietnam look more attractive as a source, but they said trading has remained relatively quiet.
Vietnam has begun harvesting rice from its winter-spring crop in the Mekong Delta and traders said quality appeared better than last year. The harvest is normally the best of the year in Vietnam.
